Playbook.name: Change Audit — FortiGate Firewall Configuration Changed - SOC Playbook

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A FortiGate configuration object was changed (Edit/Add/Move/Delete on a cfgpath). Triage question: was this a change-controlled firewall administration action, or an unexpected/unauthorized modification (e.g. opening a path an attacker needs)?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: Unauthorised firewall changes can open inbound exposure, disable protection, or exfil paths - a single rule change can breach segmentation.

Assets.AssetType: FortiGate perimeter and internal firewalls (HQ + DR)
Internal server and user segments behind the FortiGate

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: FortiGate logs shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-fortinet_fortigate.* (verified live).

Fields: fortinet.firewall.subtype (ips/dns/...), fortinet.firewall.action, fortinet.firewall.severity, fortinet.firewall.attack, fortinet.firewall.srccountry/dstcountry ('Reserved' = RFC1918 internal), fortinet.firewall.cfgpath, dns.question.name, source.ip, destination.ip, destination.port.

Input.name: $admin_ui
Input.description: Admin session origin string (fortinet.firewall.ui, e.g. 'GUI(10.0.0.5)') from the alert - FortiGate config logs carry the administrator in this field, not a user field.

Input.name: $source_ip
Input.description: Admin source IP parsed from the ui string if present.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Changes by a known firewall admin during a change window are routine; changes to security policy/address objects by an unexpected admin or outside a window need verification.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the config change is authorised administration or an unexpected modification, and what was changed.

Step.name: What configuration paths were changed and from which admin session
Step.Purpose: The cfgpath and action reveal whether security policy, VPN, or admin objects were touched (high concern) vs benign objects; ui attributes the change to an admin session/source.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE fortinet.firewall.cfgpath IS NOT NULL AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS changes = COUNT(*), paths = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.cfgpath), actions = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.action), objects = VALUES(fortinet.firewall.cfgobj), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) BY fortinet.firewall.ui | SORT changes DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: firewall.policy / firewall.address / vpn / system.admin cfgpaths are high concern. ui shows the admin session origin (GUI(ip)/jsconsole/API). A burst of changes from one session in minutes may be legitimate maintenance or an attacker reconfiguring the firewall.

Step.name: Was there an admin login/session event around the change
Step.Purpose: Correlate the change with an admin login/logout event and its UI/source to confirm the session was legitimate.
Step.Query: FROM logs-fortinet_fortigate.log-* | WHERE fortinet.firewall.action IN ("login","logout") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | KEEP @timestamp, fortinet.firewall.ui, source.ip, fortinet.firewall.action, fortinet.firewall.status | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: An admin login from an unusual source/UI (e.g. public IP, unexpected jumphost) just before the change is a red flag. fortinet.firewall.ui shows GUI/console/API origin.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows security-policy/VPN/admin-object changes by an unrecognised admin or with no change ticket.
Node.Result: True Positive (Unauthorised Firewall Change - escalate, review and revert)

Node.Condition: INV-02 shows the change followed an admin login from an unusual/public source.
INV-01 shows a known firewall admin making scoped changes during an approved window matching a ticket.
Change by a plausible admin but no ticket located.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-FGCFG-PATHS, INV-02-FGCFG-LOGIN to the case.

SOCAction.Item: Verify the change ticket; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: An unauthorised firewall configuration change (exposure, protection disable, exfil path).

SOCAction.Item: Review the changed objects; revert unauthorised changes.
Disable the admin account if compromised; open IR.
Check for new inbound exposure created by the change.

Indicators.Item: An API/automation admin per a broken job.

SOCAction.Item: Fix the automation scope; document the expected admin.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Review the changed configuration; revert if unauthorised.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Audit the full config diff; check for new exposure; reset the admin if compromised.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enforce change control + approval on firewall edits; restrict admin access to jump hosts; enable config backup/diff.

QualityChecks.Check: cfgpath present on real config events (206/7d). Include Rename per the patched rule.
Correlate with admin login (INV-02) for session context.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Authorised change confirmed; config diff benign.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Unauthorised change reverted; exposure closed; admin session investigated.
